item.title: Stephen Colbert Makes Surprise Michigan Public Access Appearance After ‘Late Show’ Farewell
item.description:
[Intro music fades out]
Host: "Welcome to our show, where we dive into the latest news and trends. Today, we're talking about Stephen Colbert's surprise appearance on a public access show in Monroe, Michigan, just two days after hosting his final episode of The Late Show with Stephen Colbert on CBS.
[Soft music plays in the background]
Host: "Colbert guest-hosted an episode of 'Only in Monroe', a Michigan public access show, which aired on Friday at 11:35 p.m. This wasn't his first time on the show, though. He previously appeared in 2015, interviewing Eminem just months before taking over The Late Show.
[Music transitions to a slightly upbeat tone]
Host: "The episode was a love letter to Michigan local culture, with Jack White serving as volunteer musical director. Jeff Daniels even made a special sandwich on the show, and Steve Buscemi appeared in a hilarious public service announcement. Colbert also caught up with Detroit native Byron Allen via FaceTime.
[Music becomes more energetic]
Host: "But the episode didn't end without a bang – literally. Colbert, White, and Daniels destroyed the set and burned it in a flaming dumpster, with Eminem giving the fire marshal's all-clear via video.
[Music fades out, and the host speaks in a more serious tone]
Host: "This came just after Colbert's 11-year run at The Late Show concluded with a finale that drew 6.74 million viewers. It's clear that Colbert is already looking to the future, and we can't wait to see what's next for him.
[Outro music starts playing]
Host: "Thanks for tuning in to our show. If you want to stay up-to-date on the latest news and trends, be sure to subscribe to our podcast and follow us on social media."
